product: Handmade craft, no brand: a yellow cardboard bee face cut-out for a Rosh Hashana photo, and a printed hexagon gift tag ('שנה טובה ומתוקה!', kindergarten name and year) attached to a wooden honey dipper.
format: hands-only DIY tutorial with voiceover and word-by-word burned-in subtitles

how_value_is_shown: A visible step-by-step craft with a finished cute result and a second, more practical idea (a printed gift tag), told in a short voiceover.
demonstration: Making both crafts in real time (cut, fold, glue, print, attach), plus a child holding the bee board.
proof: Result on screen: the finished bee board in use (the child's face is blurred) and a heap of finished gift tags.
emotion: Light, cute, warm, with a personal remark that she took the idea to a different place.
personal_story: The creator says she chose yellow and bees because it is a Rosh Hashana gift for the kindergarten, and that she turned the postcard idea into a gift tag (machine transcript).
selling_language: none (no sale); caption: 'תודו שזה הכי מתוק שיש'
captions_on_screen: burned-in subtitles of speech word by word in bold white with a dark outline at the lower center; key nouns in large purple (צילומים, לעשות, צהוב, ודבורים, הדבקות, לצלם, גלויה, תבנית, דבק)
editing_rhythm: About 8 shots in 34 s (about 4 s each); detected cuts at 0.5, 13.3, 16.7, 18.8, 29.5 and 30.8 s; no speed changes seen, the first 13 s is one continuous top-down take.
ending_and_cta: Last 3 s: hand shows the honey dipper with tag; subtitles 'מה זה', 'על המתנה', 'ספרו לי מה חשבתם' (a question to the viewer in the video), voiceover ends 'שנה טובה'. Caption: 'תודו שזה הכי מתוק שיש' with hashtags; no link or code.
convincing: Interpretation: the whole process is visible in one top-down take, the creator names the reason for each choice, and the result is cute and seasonal.
weak_or_overproduced: Interpretation: no product to buy and no CTA other than a question; hands only, so the viewer meets no face; subtitle style changes between words so it can feel busy.
lumebook_lesson: Interpretation: a one-take top-down craft or 'how I made this' format with word-by-word subtitles and a seasonal hook (Rosh Hashana, back to school) can be shot solo with a phone on a stand; LumeBook could show the steps of customizing a book the same way.
solo_without_child: yes: the tutorial is hands only; the child cameo is optional and blurred
not_verified: Whether the child in the yard shot is the creator's own; the template tool is only seen as a screen (a design editor); some machine transcript words are garbled ('סטע', 'אוספת'); borderline inclusion because it is a DIY craft rather than a commercial product.
